title: The Atlas's own research needs are duplicated verbatim under two identifiers, NR-1 and NR-8
content:
NR-1, attached under A.1.5.4 (Standard of Proof), and NR-8, attached under A.1.5.9 (Adjudication Process), are titled identically — "Systematic Basis Of Adjudication, Fact-Finding And Evidence" — and their content is word-for-word the same, from "This need is an extensive Research Track" through the closing suggestion of "independent review panels (which could operate post facto to avoid excessively delaying the deplatforming of misaligned ACs)."

This duplication is notable because the Needed Research type was designed specifically to prevent it. A.1.2.2.2.30 gives NR documents a standalone "NR-" namespace rather than deriving identifiers from a Target Document's Supporting Root, and states the reason outright: this "enables them to be linked to more than one Atlas Document, no matter the latter's location in the Atlas document tree." One research need, many links, is the intended usage — and it is exactly what this case called for, since the standard of proof and the adjudication process are two documents with the same underlying gap.

It also runs against the general normalization rule at A.1.2.2.2.22, which requires a term be defined once "at a location in the Atlas that covers all of its use" precisely because duplicates drift apart. Two copies of a research track will diverge as one is edited, and then it becomes unclear which is the live version of the question.

The practical stakes are low relative to a duplicated *rule* — nothing is adjudicated on the basis of an NR document. But it is evidence about process rather than content: the linking mechanism exists and was not used, which suggests research needs are being authored per-document by hand. In a tree where the same gap surfaces under many rules, that pattern inflates the apparent number of open questions and hides which distinct problems actually remain.
description: Both carry identical text on adjudication, fact-finding and evidence, despite Needed Research documents having standalone identifiers specifically so one need can attach to many documents.
